messages.subject: Identifying two different speakers
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am newbie to seewave as well as sound processing. I have speech data in which two different speakers have interacted with each other. Given a speech segment is it possible to say if only one of the speaker has spoken or if both of them has spoken within that time. Will it be possible to differentiate between two speakers  as well .

Thanks
Sree Viswanathan

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Identifying two different speakers
messages.body_plain:
Hi Sree,

There is definitely research going on into this sort of thing, but a good reference on speech processing would probably be a better source than the seewave list for such domain-specific information. Once you have a handle on the state of the art with respect to speaker recognition, it should be relatively straightforward to determine how/whether to do what you want with seewave.

Best,
Jesse Ross

messages.subject: Installation on OS X
messages.body_plain: Hoping to help anyone else that encountered similar troubles installing on OS X. The first issue I encountered was that the package fftw, on which seewave depends, wasn't installing. The fix for this is to install pkg-source (http://pkgconfig.freedesktop.org/). Then seewave itself didn't want to install, the solution for which was to first install libsndfile, which in turn had an error installing. There is a post here <http://stackoverflow.com/questions/20990375/fatal-error-installing-libsndfile-on-os-x-mavericks> detailing the error and an answer detailing a complicated fix, but also another answer saying to just use homebrew, which is what I did. Finally, I was able to do install.packages('seewave',type='source') in R successfully.
